title: Grateful Dead Live at University Hall, University Of Virginia on 1982-09-14
lineage: Transfer: MAC > Nakamichi CR-5A (Dolby-B in) > Edirol FA-66 > Wavelab 2448 > CD-Wave (24bit output) > TLH > FLAC 2448 tagged.
source: Source: FOB Beyers M88's > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell XLIIS-90 (1st Set, He's Gone, and JBGoode) and TDK MA-90 (2nd Set). Concert recording by Rip Tompkins, & with thanks to Richie Stankiewicz!

ai_review.summary: Excellent audience capture of a high‑energy 1982 show with rare gems like “High Time,” “Aiko Aiko,” and a stellar second set, featuring crisp stereo mix from the Beyer mic.
ai_review.review: The recording delivers an unusually clean and well‑balanced audience tape – the Beyer FO H mic work gives clear ride cymbals, correct stereo imaging and no phase problems. The performance itself is a long, high‑energy set highlighted by rare numbers (High Time, Aiko Aiko) and standout second‑set jams such as Lazy Lightning → Supplication and China > I Know You Rider.

ai_rating.rationale: All five reviews are 4–5 stars, praising both the show’s energy and the audio quality; consensus indicates an exceptional performance captured with excellent sound.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Fresh transfer from master tapes using a Beyer mic gives clear ride cymbals, accurate stereo image and on‑phase mix; FOH mixing praised, no noticeable dropouts or muffiness.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Solid, long first set with tight transitions (Jack Straw, Peggy‑O, C.C. Rider) leading into a diverse second set that flows through post‑drum segues and strong song pairings such as China > Rider and Estimated > He's Gone.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as singing from his instrument with effortless, sweet licks; guitar work praised on Deal and throughout the set.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for hitting great notes and adding high points in songs like Deal; solid bass foundation throughout.
band_member_comments.Bob: Praised for organic tone, strong vocal delivery on C.C. Rider and El Paso, and tight interplay with Jerry during jams.
